channel.title: Line by Line
channel.description: A Scripture & Exegesis Podcast searching God's Word verse by verse. Rooted in the historic, conservative Reformed tradition, each episode pairs historical-covenantal context with warm, pastoral, line-by-line exegesis drawing from classic commentaries including John Calvin, Matthew Henry, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, and Charles Spurgeon.

item.title: Matthew 26:36-46: Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane
item.description: In the fourth episode of Line by Line, host Rebecca establishes the covenantal and historical setting of our Lord's agony in Gethsemane from a conservative Reformed perspective, quoting the Berean Standard Bible. Then, George delivers a line-by-line exposition of Matthew 26:36-46, drawing from John Calvin, Matthew Henry, and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown to unpack the olive press, the cup of wrath, the sleeping disciples, and the Saviour's perfect submission to the Father's will, culminating in the comfort of Christ's finished work for His people.

item.title: James 5:12: Let Your Yes Be Yes
item.description: In the third episode of Line by Line, host Rebecca sets the historical and covenantal context of James's epistle to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, highlighting the call to patient endurance under trial. Then, George delivers a line-by-line exposition of James 5:12, drawing from John Calvin, Matthew Henry, and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown to expose the folly of evasive oaths, the sanctity of God's name, the Reformed distinction of lawful oaths, and the remedy of truthful speech, culminating in Christ the faithful and true Witness.

item.title: Psalm 1: The Two Ways and the Planted Tree
item.description: In the second episode of Line by Line, host Rebecca introduces the canonical role of Psalm 1 as the gateway to the entire Psalter from a conservative Reformed perspective. Then, George delivers a line-by-line exposition of the Hebrew text and classic commentaries of John Calvin, Matthew Henry, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, and Charles Spurgeon, contrasting the progressive downward descent of the wicked with the deeply rooted vitality of the blessed man, culminating in Christ the true Tree of Life.

item.title: Psalm 23: The Shepherd and His Sheep
item.description: In the inaugural episode of Line by Line, host Rebecca establishes the covenantal and historical setting of David's most beloved psalm from a conservative Reformed perspective. Then, George walks line-by-line through the Hebrew text and classic commentaries of John Calvin, Matthew Henry, and Charles Spurgeon, unpacking Yahweh Rohi, the valley of the shadow of death, the prepared table, and the eternal security of Christ's flock.
